subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable core logical-action idempotency and replay contract for sub-agent side effects, and what identity boundary should it use?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans agent spawn identity, gateway/tool execution, persisted session state, and external side-effect semantics; automation cannot safely choose whether to dedupe, replay, or allow repeated actions without product intent.

options.title: Design a narrow core contract
options.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, target scope, expiry, and replay behavior first, then implement the smallest core/gateway change that protects sub-agent retries.

options.title: Limit core to exact-key dedupe
options.body: Keep the existing gateway/message-tool exact-key behavior as the supported core guarantee and leave external API idempotency to workflows, plugins, and service-specific keys.

options.title: Route to ClawHub guidance
options.body: Keep core unchanged and direct unattended multi-agent operators to ClawHub skills and external-system idempotency patterns.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, target scope, expiry, and replay behavior first, then implement the smallest core/gateway change that protects sub-agent retries.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface routing signal for the subagent, gateway, and tools.invoke behavior that needs a product/API decision.
